newsitem.title: USA: LA judge recalls magazine with nude Brad Pitt pix.
newsitem.headline: LA judge recalls magazine with nude Brad Pitt pix.

text.p: A judge on Thursday ordered the recall of the latest edition of Playgirl magazine, which published photographs of movie star Brad Pitt in the nude without his permission.
But before the recall could go into effect, a lawyer for the magazine filed notice of appeal, thus placing a temporary stay on the ruling.
Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Robert O'Brien last month had stopped Playgirl from selling any more copies of the August issue, but on Thursday he went further by ordering a recall of the magazine.
Pitt has sued the magazine, alleging invasion of privacy and infliction of emotional distress for publishing the photographs. He is seeking undetermined damages.

In the suit filed on July 14 under his full name of William Bradley Pitt, the actor alleges a photographer trespassed on the grounds of a Caribbean island hotel two years ago to shoot the pictures of the actor frolicking naked.
Some of the pictures, which have been printed in European publications and appeared on the Internet, also show Pitt's former fiancee, actress Gwyneth Paltrow.
Following Thursday's recall ruling, Playgirl's attorney Kent Raygor filed notice of appeal, saying the ruling required the magazine to inform vendors and distributors and collect remaining copies.

The entire file in the case has been sealed since the lawsuit was filed by Pitt, who first rose to fame in the movie "Thelma and Louise" and has since starred in "Seven," "Interview with the Vampire," "Legends of the Fall" and "The Devil's Own."
There was no immediate reaction from Pitt's lawyers but Raygor told reporters outside the courthouse that Thursday's ruling raises "very serious First Amendment concerns."
"It restrains Playgirl's freedom of speech and censors the public's right to see information that is newsworthy and of great public interest," he said.

Saying the magazine would fight for freedom of speech, Raygor went on: "This is the first time that a California court not only has restrained the publication and sale of an entire magazine based on a few photographs appearing in it, but has gone even further and ordered the recall of a magazine that has already been mailed to subscribers and sold throughout the U.S."
